Bech32.convertBits.notes: Closest published code: exact private convertBits function extracted unchanged from bitcoin0.2.1 Segwit.mo, with attribution and SHA256 pins. Valid 8-to-5 padded conversion matches byte-for-byte; Blob-to-array and array-to-Blob adapters are timed. The plugin additionally validates bit widths and enforces16MiB input/output bounds; published private code assumes valid widths and has no such cap. This is a benchmark-only actor-private extraction, not a public package API.

BLAKE3.finalizeXof.notes: Closest published code composed from two correct public hasherFinalizeSeek calls: bytes13..63 and64..112, concatenated and converted to Blob inside timing. The pinned single call truncates at its first output-block boundary, so it cannot provide100bytes directly. This composition produces identical official-vector output without implementing compression or cryptographic state transitions. Only one1024-byte input chunk is used; this does not repair upstream multi-chunk hashing. State preparation is excluded and finalization preserves its immutable receiver.

BLAKE3.deriveKey.notes: Closest published primitives composed with two-phase domain separation: exported Hasher record/DERIVE_KEY_CONTEXT flag hash UTF8context; resulting32-byte key initializes published hasherInitKeyed with exported DERIVE_KEY_MATERIAL flag. All compression, state updates, key decoding and finalization use pinned public functions. The high-level upstream derive_key ignores context and is not used. Official BLAKE3 context/material vectors independently check this bounded composition; context and material each fit a single1024-byte chunk, so no claim is made for broken upstream multi-chunk behavior. The whole derive operation is timed.
